citations.claim: heavy body gained small +vx while light body gained large -vx; momenta do not cancel, net momentum non-zero at first violating step
light body velocity magnitude far exceeds momentum-balanced value (20x would be needed)

counterfactual.change: changed light body mass from 1 to 20 so both bodies have equal mass/acceleration and thus symmetric substepping; momentum violation disappears

explanation: With unequal masses accelerations differ 20x. The engine splits dt into substeps when bodies accelerate strongly (step 1 used 11 substeps). If substep count is chosen per-body, the heavy/low-accel body and light/high-accel body integrate with different force-evaluation histories, breaking Newton's third-law symmetry and injecting net momentum (0 initial -> ~0.246 at step 1). Equal masses give identical substep histories so symmetry is restored and the rule passes. Persistence at dt=0.001 shows it is not just coarse dt.
vision_note: Two blue bodies of clearly unequal size sit very close together near the center, with almost no visible displacement between step 0 and step 1. No ejection, explosion, or large motion is apparent at this scale despite the momentum violation.
